observations: Cast aluminum engine component with a central throttle-body bore and multiple bolt holes around the perimeter
Several ports and internal passages visible on the casting
Part is being held by hand over a wooden plank; a green bowl with tape and small items sits beneath it
Watermark text "FAMOUS AUTOS VENTURE" across the center of all three photos
No readable brand logo, part number, or model marking visible on the part in any photo
Surface shows used condition with grime and wear, but no obvious large cracks from this distance

claims.evidence: No Nissan branding or marking visible in photos 0, 1, or 2
Photos cannot confirm fuel type or engine application
Subjective claim with no supporting detail in photos
No age indicators or vintage markings visible in photos
Photos show external wear only; internal condition cannot be assessed remotely

risks.risk: Cracks in the aluminum casting, especially around thin sections or corners
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all surfaces, particularly mating faces and corners, or a light-shine video to reveal hairline cracks

risks.risk: Warped mating surfaces that will not seal properly
risks.proof: Photo of a straight edge and feeler gauge placed on the mating surface

risks.risk: Wrong fitment for the buyer's specific Nissan model
risks.proof: Legible photo of any casting number or part number, or a confirmed compatible vehicle list

risks.risk: Stripped threads or broken mounting bolt holes
risks.proof: Close-up photos of every bolt hole and threaded insert

risks.risk: Internal passage blockage or damage not visible externally
risks.proof: Borescope video or internal inspection of the throttle bore and runners

proof_requests: Close-up photos of all four sides and the mating surface
Photo of any casting numbers or part numbers on the aluminum
Photo showing a straight edge on the mating surface to check for warping
Video holding the part up to light to check for cracks
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as a used car engine intake manifold even without a readable model number, so it can be priced at its worst case (cracked, warped, wrong fitment, non-functional).
